title: Cardamom and Rose Bread-and-Butter Pudding with Raisins
summary: Overlapping triangles of buttered bread baked in a fragrant cardamom and rose custard, finished with raisins and chopped nuts.
equipment: larger roasting tin for a water bath

steps.title: Prep
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C, brush both sides of all 11 bread slices with 150 g melted butter and cut each into two triangles.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Butter a 23 x 33 cm dish, arrange the triangles overlapping with points up, then scatter in 110 g raisins, tucking some between the slices, followed by 15 g chopped pistachios and 18 g chopped almonds.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk 700 ml evaporated milk and 397 g condensed milk with 6 eggs until completely smooth, then whisk in 85 g sugar, 1 tsp cardamom, ¾ tsp nutmeg, 1 tsp rose water and 1 tsp vanilla.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Pour the custard over the bread to within 1 cm of the rim and press the slices down so they soak.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Set the dish in a roasting tin, pour boiling water in to about 1 cm deep and bake about 1 h, topping up the water as needed, until the centre reaches 71 °C and a knife comes out clean.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: If the top is pale, grill for 2-3 min, then serve warm or cold.

tips: Brush both sides of every bread slice with butter so it browns evenly and the custard soaks in all over.
Bake in a water bath and top it up if it runs low, to keep the custard setting gently rather than curdling.
safety: Check the centre reaches 71 °C and a knife comes out clean before taking the dish out of the oven.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and serve cold or reheated gently in the oven.
